en.greeting: Hi! You know is cleaned and was built. Today the passive goes further: every tense, modals, the news style It is said that…, and the verbs that can never be passive. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: One recipe, every tense
steps.text: Quick recap: passive = be + third form (is cleaned, was built), and by names the doer. Now let's take it into every tense.
steps.body:
Put **be** into the tense you need, then add the **third form**, which never changes:
- present perfect: **has/have been** + third form (*sudah di-*)
- continuous: **am/is/are/was/were being** + third form (*sedang di-*)
- future: **will be** + third form (*akan di-*)
Indonesian adds a time word to the same *di-*; English shows the time with the helper (has, is, will), so never drop it. Trick: **been** after has/have/had, **being** for *sedang*.

steps.title: The passive in every tense
steps.text: Look at the helper in each sentence: it shows the time. The last word is always the third form.
steps.body: Watch the third form: 'The email has been **send**' is a classic mistake → *has been **sent*** (send → sent → sent).

examples.en: Your order has been sent.
examples.id: Pesananmu sudah dikirim.

examples.en: Three new branches have been opened this year.
examples.id: Tiga cabang baru sudah dibuka tahun ini.

examples.en: A new bridge is being built over the river.
examples.id: Jembatan baru sedang dibangun di atas sungai.

examples.en: When I got to the office, the floor was being cleaned.
examples.id: Waktu saya sampai di kantor, lantainya sedang dibersihkan.

examples.en: The winners will be announced on Friday.
examples.id: Pemenangnya akan diumumkan hari Jumat.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You get an email from your bank.

question.prompt: Complete with the present perfect passive of 'pay': Your credit card bill ___ in full. Thank you!
question.explanation: Present perfect passive = **has + been + third form**, and pay → paid → **paid** (not 'payed'). 'has paid' is active: it says the bill paid something.

steps.title: Modals: must be done
steps.text: Harus diselesaikan, bisa dibayar, mungkin dibatalkan: how do you say these in English?
steps.body:
After a **modal** (a helper that adds meaning: *must, should, can, could, may, might*, and *have to*), the passive is **modal + be + third form**: *The report **must be finished** today.*
**The Indonesian trap:** the *di-* in *harus diselesaikan* is the part learners forget. 'must be **finish**' has no third form; 'must finished' has no be. Wherever Indonesian has *di-*, English needs **both**. Negative: *must not be used*. Question: *Can it be paid by QRIS?*

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Budi wants to take leave next week. HR tells him what to do with the leave form.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Formulirnya harus ditandatangani oleh manajermu.
question.solution: The form must be signed by your manager.
question.explanation: The thing comes first: **The form**. Then modal + be + third form: **must be signed** (harus ditandatangani), and **by** (= oleh) + the doer at the end: **your manager**.

steps.title: News style: It is said that…
steps.text: News loves konon, dikabarkan, diperkirakan. English has two passive patterns for them.
steps.body:
**1. It + is said/believed/reported + that + full sentence:** *It is said that this house is haunted.*
**2. Subject + is said/believed/thought/expected + to + verb:** *This house is said to be haunted.*
In pattern 2, use **to + base verb** for now or the future, and **to have + third form** for something **earlier**: *Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali.*
Don't mix them ('He is said **that**…') and don't add *by people*.

steps.title: In the news
steps.text: Here are both patterns in real news sentences. Notice to + verb (now/future) versus to have + third form (earlier).
steps.body: **be** shows when people said it: *It **was** reported that…* (the report was in the past).

examples.en: It was reported that twenty people were injured.
examples.id: Dikabarkan dua puluh orang terluka.

examples.en: Fuel prices are expected to rise next month.
examples.id: Harga BBM diperkirakan naik bulan depan.

examples.en: The singer is believed to be ill.
examples.id: Penyanyi itu diyakini sedang sakit.

examples.en: The fire is thought to have started in the kitchen.
examples.id: Kebakarannya diduga berawal dari dapur.

examples.en: It is estimated that 30% of the rice was lost.
examples.id: Diperkirakan 30% padinya hilang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A news report about a robbery in Jakarta.

question.prompt: Complete: The suspect ___ the country last week.
question.explanation: The leaving happened **earlier** (last week) → **to have + third form**: *is believed to have left*. 'to leave' is for now or the future, and 'is believed that he left' mixes the patterns: with *that*, start with **It**.

steps.title: No passive, and choosing
steps.text: Two last things: some verbs can never be passive, and with the others you choose.
steps.body:
Only verbs with an **object** (the thing that receives the action) can be passive. **happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise** have none. **Trap:** *terjadi* and *diadakan* look passive, but say *The accident **happened*** (not 'was happened').
**Passive:** the thing is the topic; the doer is unknown or obvious; formal style (news, notices, reports). **Active:** the doer matters; friendly chat; the doer is **you**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan's flight from Medan was two hours late.

options: The flight was arrived at 10 p.m.
The flight was arrive at 10 p.m.
question.explanation: **arrive** (tiba) has no object: nobody 'arrives' a flight, so it has no passive. Use the active: *The flight **arrived** at 10 p.m.* The other two add a *was* that English doesn't use here.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · the passive (B2)
artifact.intro: Passive = be in the tense you need + the third form, which never changes. Modals: modal + be + third form. News style: It is said that… / X is said to…
rows: It is said that the house is haunted.
X is said to + verb / to have + third form
He is said to have moved to Bali.
tips: **been** after has/have/had, **being** for the continuous, **be** after will and modals. The last word is the third form: **has been sent**, **must be finished** (not 'send', 'finish').
No object, no passive: **happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, disappear, rise**. *The accident happened*, not 'was happened', even though *terjadi* looks passive.
Passive for the topic, an unknown or obvious doer and formal writing; active when the doer matters, in chat, and when the doer is **you**.

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah kenal is cleaned dan was built. Hari ini passive melangkah lebih jauh: semua tense, modal, gaya berita It is said that…, dan kata kerja yang tidak pernah bisa pasif. Yuk, langkah demi langkah.

steps.title: Satu resep, semua tense
steps.text: Ringkasan singkat: passive = be + bentuk ketiga (is cleaned, was built), dan by menyebut pelakunya. Sekarang kita bawa ke semua tense.
steps.body:
Ubah **be** ke tense yang kamu perlukan, lalu tambahkan **bentuk ketiga**, yang tidak pernah berubah:
- present perfect: **has/have been** + bentuk ketiga (*sudah di-*)
- continuous: **am/is/are/was/were being** + bentuk ketiga (*sedang di-*)
- future: **will be** + bentuk ketiga (*akan di-*)
Bahasa Indonesia menambah kata waktu ke *di-* yang sama; bahasa Inggris menunjukkan waktunya lewat kata bantu (has, is, will), jadi jangan dibuang. Triknya: **been** setelah has/have/had, **being** untuk *sedang*.

steps.title: Passive di semua tense
steps.text: Perhatikan kata bantu di setiap kalimat: kata itu menunjukkan waktunya. Kata terakhirnya selalu bentuk ketiga.
steps.body: Perhatikan bentuk ketiganya: 'The email has been **send**' adalah kesalahan klasik → *has been **sent*** (send → sent → sent).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu menerima email dari bankmu.

question.prompt: Lengkapi dengan present perfect passive dari 'pay': Your credit card bill ___ in full. Thank you!
question.explanation: Present perfect passive = **has + been + bentuk ketiga**, dan pay → paid → **paid** (bukan 'payed'). 'has paid' itu aktif: artinya tagihannya yang membayar sesuatu.

steps.title: Modal: must be done
steps.text: Harus diselesaikan, bisa dibayar, mungkin dibatalkan: bagaimana mengatakannya dalam bahasa Inggris?
steps.body:
Setelah **modal** (kata bantu yang menambah makna: *must, should, can, could, may, might*, dan *have to*), passive-nya adalah **modal + be + bentuk ketiga**: *The report **must be finished** today.*
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia:** *di-* dalam *harus diselesaikan* adalah bagian yang sering dilupakan. 'must be **finish**' tidak punya bentuk ketiga; 'must finished' tidak punya be. Setiap ada *di-*, bahasa Inggris perlu **dua-duanya**. Negatif: *must not be used*. Tanya: *Can it be paid by QRIS?*

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Budi mau cuti minggu depan. HRD menjelaskan apa yang harus dilakukan dengan formulir cutinya.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Formulirnya harus ditandatangani oleh manajermu.
question.solution: The form must be signed by your manager.
question.explanation: Bendanya di depan: **The form**. Lalu modal + be + bentuk ketiga: **must be signed** (harus ditandatangani), dan **by** (= oleh) + pelakunya di akhir: **your manager**.

steps.title: Gaya berita: It is said that…
steps.text: Berita suka memakai konon, dikabarkan, diperkirakan. Bahasa Inggris punya dua pola passive untuk itu.
steps.body:
**1. It + is said/believed/reported + that + kalimat lengkap:** *It is said that this house is haunted.*
**2. Subjek + is said/believed/thought/expected + to + kata kerja:** *This house is said to be haunted.*
Di pola 2, pakai **to + bentuk dasar** untuk sekarang atau nanti, dan **to have + bentuk ketiga** untuk sesuatu yang **lebih dulu**: *Pak Hasan is said to have moved to Bali.*
Jangan campur keduanya ('He is said **that**…') dan jangan tambah *by people*.

steps.title: Di berita
steps.text: Ini kedua pola dalam kalimat berita sungguhan. Perhatikan to + kata kerja (sekarang/nanti) dibandingkan to have + bentuk ketiga (lebih dulu).
steps.body: **be** menunjukkan kapan orang mengatakannya: *It **was** reported that…* (laporannya di masa lalu).

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sebuah berita tentang perampokan di Jakarta.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: The suspect ___ the country last week.
question.explanation: Kepergiannya terjadi **lebih dulu** (last week) → **to have + bentuk ketiga**: *is believed to have left*. 'to leave' untuk sekarang atau nanti, dan 'is believed that he left' mencampur kedua pola: kalau pakai *that*, mulai dengan **It**.

steps.title: Tanpa pasif, dan memilih
steps.text: Dua hal terakhir: ada kata kerja yang tidak pernah bisa pasif, dan untuk yang lain kamu yang memilih.
steps.body:
Hanya kata kerja yang punya **objek** (benda yang dikenai tindakan) yang bisa pasif. **happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, appear, disappear, rise** tidak punya objek. **Jebakan:** *terjadi* dan *diadakan* terlihat pasif, tapi bilang *The accident **happened*** (bukan 'was happened').
**Passive:** bendanya jadi topik; pelakunya tidak diketahui atau sudah jelas; gaya formal (berita, pengumuman, laporan). **Aktif:** pelakunya penting; obrolan santai; pelakunya **kamu sendiri**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pesawat Pak Hasan dari Medan terlambat dua jam.

options: The flight was arrived at 10 p.m.
The flight was arrive at 10 p.m.
question.explanation: **arrive** (tiba) tidak punya objek: tidak ada orang yang 'arrive' sebuah pesawat, jadi tidak ada bentuk pasifnya. Pakai bentuk aktif: *The flight **arrived** at 10 p.m.* Dua pilihan lainnya menambahkan *was* yang tidak dipakai di sini.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · passive (B2)
artifact.intro: Passive = be dalam tense yang kamu perlukan + bentuk ketiga, yang tidak pernah berubah. Modal: modal + be + bentuk ketiga. Gaya berita: It is said that… / X is said to…
rows: It is said that the house is haunted.
X is said to + kata kerja / to have + bentuk ketiga
He is said to have moved to Bali.
tips: **been** setelah has/have/had, **being** untuk continuous, **be** setelah will dan modal. Kata terakhirnya bentuk ketiga: **has been sent**, **must be finished** (bukan 'send', 'finish').
Tanpa objek, tanpa pasif: **happen, occur, take place, arrive, die, disappear, rise**. *The accident happened*, bukan 'was happened', walaupun *terjadi* terlihat pasif.
Passive untuk topik, pelaku yang tidak diketahui atau sudah jelas, dan tulisan formal; aktif kalau pelakunya penting, dalam obrolan, dan kalau pelakunya **kamu sendiri**.
